dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For each natural number n, this is the bundled type of runs constructed by D008. A run contains n-dimensional matrices and vectors, iteration-indexed sequences, real error parameters, coefficient sequences, and proofs of all conditions listed in D008.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The target quantifies over every such bundled run. Consequently all constructor conditions are implicit hypotheses of the proposition; for dimensions admitting no run, the universal assertion is vacuous.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a run and iteration i, this is u_S times [1 plus (1+u_S) times eta_i], where eta_i is D014.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the coefficient multiplying the current true residual norm on the right-hand side.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: For iteration i, this is (1+u_S eta_i)(1+u_S) gamma_m(u_R)(norm(b)+norm(A) norm(x_i)) + u norm(A) norm(x_{i+1}), with eta_i from D014, m from D017, gamma from D013, and the vector and matrix norms from D005 and D015.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the complete additive error term in the residual bound.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: The true residual vector at iteration i: its j-th coordinate is b_j minus the j-th coordinate of A x_i.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The target compares the infinity norm of the true residual at i+1 with that at i.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: The norm of a real-valued function on Fin n under the finite product norm; mathematically this is the vector infinity norm max_j |x_j|, with value zero for an empty index type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets every vector norm in the target and in the bundled assumptions as an infinity norm.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projection of the matrix A from a bundled run.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It identifies the matrix used in residuals, matrix-vector products, norms, sparsity counts, and error terms.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef007
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projection of the right-hand-side vector b from a bundled run.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It identifies the vector used in the residual, sparsity parameter, and additive error term.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef008
dependency_coverage.meaning: The constructor for a run. It takes n>0; matrices A and Ainv; a vector b; sequences x, rHat, dHat, deltaR, and deltaX; real numbers u_R, u, u_S, and u_F; and nonnegative sequences c1 and c2. It requires 0<=u_R<=u<=u_S<=u_F, m u_R<1, Ainv(Az)=z for every vector z, rHat_i=b-Ax_i+deltaR_i, the stated componentwise deltaR bound, the stated normwise inexact-solve bound, x_{i+1}=x_i+dHat_i+deltaX_i, the componentwise deltaX bound, and c1_i norm(Ainv) norm(A) u_S<1 for every i.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: These data and proofs are all encoded in the quantified run and therefore act as the proposition's hypotheses, even though the target has no explicit implication.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef009
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projection of the real parameter u from a bundled run.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It appears in the final term u norm(A) norm(x_{i+1}) and in the componentwise update-error hypothesis.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef010
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projection of the real parameter u_R from a bundled run.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the argument of gamma_m and is constrained by 0<=u_R and m u_R<1.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef011
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projection of the real parameter u_S from a bundled run.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It occurs throughout both coefficients, their denominator condition, and several bundled error assumptions.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef012
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projection of the sequence x: Nat -> Fin n -> Real from a bundled run.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the current and next iterates x_i and x_{i+1}.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef013
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a real u and natural number k, gamma_k(u) = (k u)/(1-k u), where k is cast to a real number.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With k=m from D017 and u=u_R, it contributes the factor gamma_m(u_R) to the additive residual error.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef014
dependency_coverage.meaning: For iteration i, eta_i = (c1_i kappa + c2_i)/(1-c1_i kappa u_S), where kappa=norm(Ainv) norm(A).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It enters both the current-residual coefficient and the leading factor of the additive error term.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef015
dependency_coverage.meaning: The matrix infinity operator norm. For a real n by n matrix A, this is max_j sum_k |A_{jk}|.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef016

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef017

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef018

binders: n is an implicitly universally quantified natural number, and I_n=Fin n is the coordinate set {0,...,n-1}.

run is an arbitrary bundled n-dimensional run. Unpacked, it contains A,B in Real^{n by n}; b in Real^n; sequences x, rHat, dHat, deltaR, deltaX from Nat to Real^n; real parameters u_R,u,u_S,u_F; sequences c1,c2 from Nat to Real; and proofs of the hypotheses below. Here B denotes the field called Ainv.
i is an arbitrary natural-number iteration index, with no upper bound or relation to n.
hypotheses: For every iteration k, c1_k>=0 and c2_k>=0.
Let m=max_{j in I_n}(#{l in I_n:A_{jl}!=0}+1_{b_j!=0}); then m u_R<1.
B is an exact left inverse of A: B(Az)=z for every z in Real^n.
For every k and j, rHat_{k,j}=b_j-(A x_k)_j+deltaR_{k,j}.
For every k, c1_k kappa u_S<1, where kappa=||B||_infinity||A||_infinity.
conclusions: For every iteration i, ||b-Ax_{i+1}||_infinity <= u_S[1+(1+u_S)eta_i]||b-Ax_i||_infinity + (1+u_S eta_i)(1+u_S)gamma_m(u_R)[||b||_infinity+||A||_infinity||x_i||_infinity] + u||A||_infinity||x_{i+1}||_infinity.
mathematical_definitions: For z in Real^n, (Az)_j=sum_{l in I_n} A_{jl}z_l, and similarly for Bz.
For v in Real^n, ||v||_infinity=max_{j in I_n}|v_j|.
For an n by n real matrix M, ||M||_infinity=max_{j in I_n}sum_{l in I_n}|M_{jl}|.
The true residual at iteration k is r_k=b-Ax_k.
The entrywise absolute-value product is (|A||x_k|)_j=sum_{l in I_n}|A_{jl}||x_{k,l}|.
gamma_m(u_R)=m u_R/(1-m u_R), with m interpreted as a real number.
The coefficient of the current residual is u_S[1+(1+u_S)eta_i].
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every bundled run satisfying the stated positivity, inverse, residual-computation, inexact-solve, iterate-update, perturbation, and denominator conditions, and for every natural iteration i, the infinity norm of the true residual at the next iterate is at most a specified multiple of the current true residual norm plus a data-and-current-iterate error term and the additional term u times the matrix infinity norm times the next-iterate infinity norm. The coefficients are exactly those obtained from the sparsity-dependent quantity gamma_m(u_R) and eta_i=(c1_i||B||_infinity||A||_infinity+c2_i)/(1-c1_i||B||_infinity||A||_infinity u_S).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The proposition does not assert that any bundled run exists. It is vacuously true for any n for which LocalDef001 n is empty.
In particular, n=0 admits no constructor because every run carries a proof of 0<n, so the n=0 case is vacuous.
All substantive assumptions are hidden inside the type of run rather than displayed as antecedents of the target.
The iteration index i ranges over every natural number. No stopping time, finite iteration range, or relation i<n is encoded.

The strict assumptions m u_R<1 and c1_i kappa u_S<1 make the denominators in gamma_m(u_R) and eta_i positive for every bundled run. Lean's division itself is total, but these guards exclude zero denominators here.
The statement is only a one-step residual bound. It does not assert that the residual coefficient is below one, that the residuals converge, or that the iterates converge.
The matrix B is explicitly assumed only to satisfy the left-inverse identity B(Az)=z for all z; the proposition does not separately state a right-inverse identity.
The auxiliary sequences rHat, dHat, deltaR, and deltaX do not occur in the final inequality, but their globally quantified equations and bounds restrict which runs exist.
The parameter u_F does not occur in the conclusion except indirectly through the bundled ordering condition u_S<=u_F; no assumption u_F<1 is encoded.
No probabilistic, asymptotic, floating-point-format, termination, or algorithm-identification claim is encoded beyond the exact deterministic equations and inequalities listed.
The assumptions on residual computation, solves, updates, and denominator guards hold for every natural iteration, which is stronger than requiring them only at the particular target index i.
